newsitem.title: USA: Clinton works hard to get his knee better.
newsitem.headline: Clinton works hard to get his knee better.

text.p: A month after knee surgery, President Bill Clinton is deep into a rehabilitation regimen that aides say he is approaching like he does everything else -- energetically.
Rather than gain weight as many people do when they are sidelined with a serious injury, Clinton is said to have actually lost five pounds on a low-calorie, high-carbohydrate diet.

He can sometimes be seen shambling around the White House grounds on his black, lightweight crutches. On Friday, he was spotted walking from the north entrance across the front lawn to the Old Executive Office Building next door.
He has also been walking around the cushioned jogging path that was put around the driveway on the south lawn but has not not gotten much use because Clinton tended to jog elsewhere in the capital.

Upstairs in the White House residence, he has been working out in a gym facility, concentrating on increasing his upper body strength. Aides said he will sometimes pedal one-legged with his good leg on a stationery bike. For his injured leg there is regular physical therapy.
He was hoping soon to go swimming in the White House pool.
Said one White House official: "My sense is that, as with everything he does, he is not only going at it full bore but is fascinated by learning about the process."

The 50-year-old Clinton hurt his knee March 14 in a middle-of-the-night stumble at the Florida estate of golf pro Greg Norman. It happened at a time when Clinton was trying to get his golf game in form for the summer months.
Now all he can do is gaze wistfully at the White House putting green, and watch the Masters golf tournament on television.

"I have about a minimum of four months and probably a couple more weeks before I can play golf. So it's a long way away," he told reporters during a picture-taking session Tuesday with a man he wanted to play golf with, Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien.

Clinton tends to dwell on his plight in public remarks. He joked about his leg frequently in a remarks at the annual dinner of Washington radio and television reporters Thursday night. He laughingly compared himself to former President George Bush, who had recently parachuted from a plane.
"I mean, look at this, this guy is 72 years old, he jumps out of a plane at 12,000 feet, he lands without a scratch. I fall six inches and I am crippled up for six months. It's ridiculous," he said.
So far, Clinton does not appear to be letting the injury get him down, however.

"There was all this speculation that he would get all cranky and things like that," said White House spokesman Mike McCurry. "I think he is interested in the challenge of getting better and meeting the requirements of the regimen he's in and sees it as an opportunity to do some other things."
Said another official: "Everyone is trying very hard to keep his spirits up."

McCurry said Clinton has been studying even more than usual, reading a lot and playing cards with his wife Hillary and daughter Chelsea, as well as helping her in choosing which university she will attend next year.
"He can tell you in extraordinary amount about the way in which the Consumer Price Index is calculated," McCurry said.
